housing: Stroud is a district of Cotswold stone towns in the Five Valleys, with old mill buildings, steep terraced streets and many listed or conservation-area homes. Private renting is below the national average, with lets concentrated in Stroud, Stonehouse, Dursley and Cam. Large new-build estates have been added around Stonehouse, Cam and the edge of Gloucester. Rural villages have stone cottages, some off the gas grid.
checkinTips: Cotswold stone cottages and terraces: photograph thick walls, window reveals and any damp patches or flaking limewash.
Hillside homes in Stroud and Nailsworth: record steps, retaining walls, sloping gardens and access paths.
Converted mill flats in the valleys: note shared entrances, lifts, parking and any signs of damp near the water.
Rural homes off the gas grid: photograph the oil tank or LPG supply, fuel level and boiler service label.
New-build estates at Great Oldbury and Cam: note snagging marks, fences, turf and allocated parking.
tenantHelp: Private tenants can contact Stroud District Council's Private Sector Housing team about disrepair, damp and unsafe conditions.
